newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline shares dip from record highs.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline shares dip from record highs.

text.p: Shares in SmithKline Beecham Plc dipped on Friday but held the bulk of their gains of the past two sessions, fired by speculation of a bid from Roche Holding AG or a merger with the Swiss firm.
SmithKline shares were down 7p at 823-1/2 by 0910 GMT, after leaping 51-1/2p in the past two sessions to a record high. Trading was active with volume reaching 1.1 million shares.
Traders and analysts have been sceptical of the chances of a bid for SmithKline but said there was still scope for consolidation in the world pharmaceutical industry.
"I think a lot of people expect Roche to expand through acquisition, but then again they have been expecting it for the whole of 1996," said one senior sales trader.
"We don't feel that the rationalisation in the pharmaceutical sector has finished and there could be a further round of bids and mergers."
"Even the largest company in the world by sales, Glaxo Wellcome, only has a small share of the global market and some of the mergers we have seen have shown there are real cost savings to be made."
